title: DeploymentPluginOptions
summary: Configure public deployment metadata and optional private route templates.

sections.title: manifestURL
sections.body: Override the URL read by watchDeployment. manifestFile selects the emitted filename, defaulting to ${namespace}-manifest.json. Extensionless names such as __appm are supported. Your host must serve that file at the configured URL. Omit the override for an absolute Vite base, or set it explicitly for multiple applications, a CDN or relative bases.

sections.title: Server compatibility
sections.body: compatibility contributes to build and shared fingerprints. Change it for incompatible independently deployed server contracts or external runtime configuration that the browser graph cannot observe. It does not substitute for retaining old assets or consistent deployment ordering.

sections.title: When to change the compatibility key
sections.body: Usually no key is needed: changes visible to the browser build already change its fingerprints. Use a stable contract identifier only for incompatible changes outside that graph, then rebuild and deploy the frontend and its manifest with the new key. For example, an independently deployed API changing { name } to { displayName } is invisible to an unchanged browser build. A new key makes old tabs eligible for recovery; the newly deployed frontend must already understand the new response. It does not repair incompatible code, detect backend deployments automatically, or replace coordinated rollout and backward compatibility. Do not change the key for ordinary data updates.

sections.title: Public and private metadata
sections.body: manifestMode: version-only omits shared/per-route fingerprints from both the public manifest and the virtual browser metadata. privateManifestFile writes generated route templates outside client output and publicDir; keep it outside every static hosting root. These settings do not remove route definitions from application code or implement authorization-aware route discovery.
